abstract: This article presents a three-phase single-stage photovoltaic energy conversion system (PECS) that connects residential buildings (RB) to the power grid. Unlike the traditional use of RBs as power consumers, this system treats RBs as power generators. However, PECS lacks inertia, making integrating with the power grid challenging. Addressing the issue, the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technique is used to add inertia to the PECS-based system. The main focus of the article is to enhance the grid’s interactivity by introducing Residential Building Virtual Synchronous Generators (RBVSG). RBVSG is tested under distorted grid voltage and varying load conditions, proving its ability to provide distortion-free, balanced grid currents with adjustable power factor while maintaining power quality. In low solar power availability, RBVSG continues to enhance power quality and imports power from the utility grid to meet local demands. Furthermore, under such conditions, the PECS power reduces or has a huge deviation in voltage; the dc-link voltage adjusts adaptively by following the variations in grid voltage, thereby increasing RBVSG system reliability and reducing operating losses. The system’s efficacy is checked in MATLAB/Simulink platform and experimentally validated by a laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: A Model Predictive Control-based Flexible Power Point Tracker for Grid-tied Photovoltaic Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: In distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems, the grid operator may impose the limit of power injected by the PV system at the point of common coupling. This power limit might be lower than the power generated by the PV system during the peak generation hour. In this work, we propose a flexible power point tracking (FPPT) method based on model predictive control for grid-connected photovoltaic inverters. A finite control set-model predictive controller (FCS-MPC) for the control of the inverter DC bus voltage and the grid current is employed to operate at the desired reference voltage set by the FPPT algorithm and inject the desired PV-generated power into the utility grid. The grid-side controller injects the power with a unity power factor using the voltage-oriented control principle in a rotational d-q reference frame. The rotation of the d-q reference frame is synchronized by the phase-locked loop algorithm. The validity of the proposed control system is confirmed through experimental tests conducted with the aid of solar array and grid simulators, a microlabbox controller, and a two-level inverter paired with an R-L filter.

articleTitle: Investigating A Clean Natural Gas-based Hydrogen Production Process for Electricity Generation in Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This study investigates a clean hydrogen production process (based on a CH4 feedstock flow rate of 1000 kmol/h) integrated with an onsite hydrogen-combustion power plant. A rate-based kinetic model is used to develop steam methane reforming (SMR) and water gas shift (WGS) reactions in the reformer. The impact of auto thermal reforming (ATR) on hydrogen purity and the generated power is investigated by analysing the correlation between temperature, pressure, and steam-to-methane ratio. A full factorial design matrix is used to investigate the potential interactions among the operational variables with a set of key performance indicators (KPIs) i.e. hydrogen purity and generated power. The ATR leads to higher hydrogen purity and generated power at lower feed temperatures Also, increasing the steam-to-methane ratio leads to increased hydrogen purity and generated power in both scenarios. Pressure is found to play a critical role in power generation but has a less pronounced effect on hydrogen purity in comparison. Employment of ATR has been found to be beneficial to achieve higher hydrogen purity and increased power generated at lower feed temperatures, while simultaneously minimizing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions.

articleTitle: Development of High Renewable Penetration Test Cases for Dynamic Network Simulations using a Synthetic Model of South-East Australia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Power system studies rely on trusted benchmark models to test new theories and technologies. While many such models exist for small networks, realistic benchmark models for full-scale networks tend to be less available due to data confidentiality. Synthetic models offer a potential solution to this issue by allowing the public release of network models through data obfuscation. One such model, of Australia’s National Electricity Market transmission network, has recently been made publicly available, however, it lacks details of inverter-based generation that are required for dynamic modeling. In this paper, the synthetic model is extended to include parameter values for inverter-based generators that are required for electromechanical dynamic modelling and 25 operating conditions with varying penetrations of inverter-based generation are identified based on future network expansion plans. The steady-state and dynamic performances of the derived model and operating points are analyzed.

articleTitle: Three Phase PFC Rectifier Control Design Using Harmonic Current Injection Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This article proposes a control design of the three-phase PFC rectifier using triangle current and third-order current. The three-phase PFC rectifier was chosen among the other topologies because of the advantage of lower switch count, higher quality input current, and small DC-link capacitor requirement. The complete steady state analysis of this three phase PFC rectifier is explained, and after that appropriate duty is derived for the inductor current reference and finally the control of the inductor current is achieved. Two different currents, third order and triangle current are generated and tracked successfully with the help of proper duty and PI control. The PFC rectifier is analyzed for two different current signals and for two other load conditions. The MATLAB® simulation results have been shown for the verification of the study.

articleTitle: A Gaussian Mixture Model and Conditional Generative Adversarial Network based Hybrid Method for Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting of Offshore Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Improving the accuracy of short-term offshore wind power prediction is extremely important for the integration of wind power generation into the electricity grid. Therefore, a short-term forecasting method of offshore wind power is proposed combining Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) in this paper. The datasets of an offshore wind farm with 15 wind turbines collected by a supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system are first analyzed and preprocessed. A GMM clustering method based on data distribution is then used to cluster the wind turbines and determine the best grouping scheme, and the forecasting model CGAN designed with the convolutional neural network (CNN) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) is constructed for each group separately. Finally, taking the processed data as a practical example, forecasting results indicate that the proposed GMM-CGAN-based method can effectively predict the day-ahead hourly actual power output of the offshore wind farm, and provide higher accuracy compared with the other forecasting methods.

articleTitle: Very short-term prediction of photovoltaic energy in the winter building for an automatic energy management system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: In the context of the energy transition, renewable energies have an important role to play. This is particularly true of photovoltaic (PV) energy. The use of PV energy in buildings is becoming increasingly common nowadays. Buildings integrated PV (BIPV) represent a major advantage in this respect, thanks to their high PV energy harvesting capacity. However, the amount of PV energy is not fixed, since it depends on the climate. Therefore, it is essential to have effective means of predicting production in advance. This will enable us to arrange before we run out of electricity. In this paper, we propose deep learning models to predict PV energy. These are the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). We have also used a hybrid model combining these two types of models. We propose a very short-term prediction, corresponding to a prediction every 5 minutes in advance. The advantage of this type of prediction is that we can propose a means of automating the power supply to the building in question according to the predicted result. To this end, we discuss future perspectives with the focus on the automation power supply. This study was applied in a Positive Energy Winter House (PEWH). The data collected from this building enabled us to develop our artificial intelligence models for PV prediction . Our study shows that the combination of models performs better in very short term PV energy prediction for winter buildings using the univariate approach.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Grid-Synchronization: A Tracking-Filter In-the-Loop Apporach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a robust three-phase grid-synchronization scheme using tracking filters. The proposed scheme falls under the category of Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) synchronization methodologies and employs a SRF-Phase Locked Loop (SRF-PLLs) structure with specifically designed building blocks. To ensure the convergence of the estimated grid angle under non-ideal input signal conditions, including DC bias and harmonics, a series of filters and signal conditioning techniques are employed. The performance of the proposed grid-synchronization scheme has been evaluated through testing under common grid disturbances, including frequency and angle jumps in the input signals.

articleTitle: Resilience-Driven Distribution Network Optimization with BESS and EV Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This work aims to achieve the Level 1 Resilience criteria during extreme situations, such as natural disasters, by harnessing the potential of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Electric Vehicles (EV). Unlike existing literature, this work proposes connecting optimal critical loads at every bus in the distribution network through a mixed integer nonlinear optimization problem (MINLP). Optimal placement of EV fleets and BESS is also proposed for loss minimization in the network. Further, the optimal discharge limit for the BESS and EV, during normal conditions is calculated by formulating an MINLP for cost minimization. The energy equivalent of the remainder State of Charge (SOC) post optimal discharge is reserved to be utilized only during resiliency conditions, as executed in the proposed energy management scheme. Hence, the goals of resiliency enhancement and economic feasibility are met concomitantly. All optimization formulations have been executed in General Algebraic Modelling System (GAMS). Finally, the proposed resiliency enhancement model is validated on a modified IEEE 33 bus distribution system in MATLAB/ SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: A Lifetime Prediction Approach Based on Adversarial Variational Auto-Encoder Networks for Dry-Type Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Remaining useful lifetime prediction provides effective means for reasonable lifetime extension and safe functioning of power transformers and supports stable operation and maintenance for power grids. To address the problems of data limitation and massive capital and labor consumptions in traditional prediction methods, a novel power transformer life prediction approach based on Adversarial Variational Auto-encoder(AVAE) is proposed in this paper. Feature extraction and data enhancement are performed by a variational auto-encoder. Adversarial training network is implemented to obtain data- driven in global optimum conditions. Furthermore, Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) network is utilized to efficiently extract the long-term dependencies in the transformer time series data, which in turn achieves the aging rate prediction. Real data of power transformers are employed for the experiments. The experimental results show that the prediction algorithm based on AVAE-LSTM networks possesses higher accuracy compares to the conventional methods.

articleTitle: A Three-Port DC-DC Converter for Solar PV Integration in DC Off-Grid Systems: Design and Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: In dc off-grid systems, each solar photovoltaic (PV) source is conventionally connected in parallel to the dc bus using a second-order boost converter which also performs maximum power point tracking (MPPT). However, this requires multiple dc-dc converters leading to higher component count, lower system efficiency, sub-system interactions, etc. In order to obviate these issues a three-port (double input and single output) fifth-order dc-dc boost converter (FOTPC) is proposed and analyzed, in this paper, for interfacing a couple of solar PV sources with a dc bus in an off-grid systems. The converter has two switches that can be individually controlled to regulate the maximum power point of both solar panels over a wider range of PV voltage and current variation. The operating modes of the converter are described for power extraction from both sources. The paper also presents the steady-state and time-domain analysis of the converter in continuous-conduction mode. Small-signal discrete-time model of FOTPC is developed and used for controller design and stability analysis. The converter operation is validated on a 48 V bus system with nominal power of 200 W.

articleTitle: Current Control Strategy using Sinusoidal Signal Integrators for Harmonic Elimination in a Standalone Microgird
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This study deals with the control of a standalone microgrid formed by solar photovoltaic (PV) and a self-excited induction generator (SEIG)-based micro-hydro renewable energy sources (RESs) feeding balanced three-phase non-linear (NL) loads at the point of common coupling (PCC). A voltage source inverter (VSI) is connected to the PCC to regulate the microgrid’s voltage. The VSI control is implemented through cascade control of the outer voltage proportional-integral (PI) controller and inner current control strategy (CCS). CCS is implemented by proportional-sinusoidal signal integrator (SSI) for fundamental frequency (ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) in the stationary frame. The VSI also eliminates dominant harmonics injected by the NL loads by implementing multiple SSIs with frequency 6kω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in a synchronous frame rotating at the fundamental frequency. It helps in reducing the computational burden as a single SSI compensates for both (6k±1)ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> harmonics. A battery energy storage system (BESS) at the DC-link of the VSI maintains the active power balance between generated and consumed power, which regulates the microgrid frequency. The performance of the proposed control is evaluated by simulating it on the MATLAB platform with both generation and load change, even during unbalanced loading conditions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Over Current Protection of SPV Integrated Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The integration of solar photovoltaic (SPV) system to conventional grid causes various protection challenges in the distribution systems. These challenges arise due to modified network topologies, limited fault current contribution, and bidirectional power flows. The low fault current contribution of inverter-based resources is due to the thermal constraints of converter switches. The reduction in current contribution from inverter-based sources causes the maloperation of conventional over-current relaying schemes in the distribution system. Also, the varying load levels limit the operation of conventional voltage-restrained relays. In this paper, a new methodology is developed to mitigate the issues of existing over-current relays (OCRs). This approach uses local positive sequence current and voltage to modify the pickup current of the relay and makes it adaptive to different loading conditions. In this work, the SPV plant model is operated in voltage control mode where the SPV plant complies with grid codes, i.e., the fault ride-through (FRT) condition. The methodology developed is validated on an IEEE 9-bus system in PSCAD platform. Hardware-in-the-loop testing using Speedgoat real-time simulator as power system and Texas Instruments launchpad as relay validates the performance of the proposed method in real-time.

articleTitle: Advanced Nonlinear Backstepping Controller for Magnetic Linked DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: An advanced nonlinear backstepping controller is proposed in this paper for magnetic-linked dc-dc converter to accomplish robust voltage regulation with less settling time and zero steady stare error without any chattering effect. The efficacy of the suggested controller is assessed in a variety of operational scenarios, including changes in load, input voltage, and step changes in the reference signal for the controller. The proposed controller provides a control equation with only one gain parameter facilitating easy tuning capability. In order to compare, the performance of the suggested controller is investigated with the most common proportional-integral controller and several nonlinear sliding mode controllers, like no integral sliding mode controller and double integral sliding mode controller. All the outcomes of different case studies validated the superior performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Reactive power compensator placement using flower pollination algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Reactive power compensator placement is challenging in distribution systems due to several complex factors and considerations, specifically the complex topology of the distribution network and it involves non-convex optimization problems. Therefore, in this study, the allocation of reactive power compensation devices is proposed by using a flower pollination algorithm (FPA) for decreasing active power losses in a distribution network. The objective of this work is to minimalize the total network power losses by optimally defining the position and capacity of the reactive power compensators, in addition to improving the voltage profile. The proposed approach was applied at the IEEE 33 bus radial distribution network (RDN) for single and multi-units compensation. The results attained are compared with several recent optimization approaches. The results show that FPA is an effectual optimization method for finding solutions for reactive compensator placement issues.

articleTitle: Least-squares estimation of power law for aggregation of harmonic currents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: A critical choice when modelling wind farms, solar farms, BESS installations and other inverter-based resources (IBRs) for harmonic penetration studies is the approach to combining harmonic currents from many identical units, to obtain the best estimate of the equivalent aggregate current at the point of connection. The long-standing practice based on the IEC ‘second summation law’ has been called into question by observations on single-phase AC string inverters at a US solar farm site. Many practitioners therefore advocate a conservative approach where no diversity in current phase angles is assumed and current magnitudes are purely additive. In this paper, a straightforward analysis of data collected by a solar inverter OEM is offered as evidence that the IEC summation law provides realistic estimates of aggregate harmonic currents from solar farms, and conversely, there is a reasonable likelihood that the conservative approach leads to inefficient design and unnecessary costs.

articleTitle: Fuel Cell System Operation as a Static Synchronous Series Compensator for Implementing Power Flow Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Due to the advancements in technology, the demand for electric power keeps on increasing, which further leads to voltage stability problems. Another undesirable effect is an increase in the transmission line losses in a heavily loaded transmission network. Furthermore, it alters the active and reactive power flows in the line. One of the solutions to this problem is the effective implementation of flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) devices. These devices can control power flow in the transmission system to improve asset utilization. In this paper, the modeling and design of the hydrogen fuel cell system-based static synchronous series compensator (SSSC) is developed for regulating the power flow in the transmission line. To validate the proposed work, a two-bus system with different configurations is designed and simulated with and without a compensator in a MATLAB/Simulink platform. The simulated results comply and validate the theoretical development of fuel cell-based SSSC proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Variable Speed Pumped Storage Hydropower Plant for Black Start
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper explores the power system restoration capability of large pumped storage variable speed hydropower plant, by operating it as a black start unit. A 250MW wound rotor induction generator, initially charged by a battery energy storage, circuit breakers and converters assembly are considered as the black start unit. The fast-starting pumped storage plant has completely governable mechanical input which navigates to speedy power built-up by the generator. The voltage and frequency stability is achieved by grid forming control of hydropower generator. Long transmission lines can be energized, as they can support huge reactive power. This helps in restoration of grid. The rotor accepts initial magnetizing and slip power from the battery and once the transmission lines are energized, the grid side converters and DC link capacitor can be switched in and battery can be removed. MATLAB simulations are carried out for the black start by energizing transmission lines, resistive and highly inductive loads. The results verify the black start potential of pumped storage hydropower plant.

articleTitle: Thermal Design via Improved Force-Directed Algorithm for IGCT Driver Board
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The power electronic device integrated gate commutated thyristor (IGCT) is currently being developed towards higher power density and reliability. As a crucial part of the IGCT, a highly integrated driver board is essential for the reliable turn-on and turn-off of the IGCT. However, thermal failure is the primary cause of failure for the IGCT driver board. Therefore, a reasonable thermal design of the driver board is imperative for the reliability of the IGCT. This paper proposes an improved force-directed algorithm suitable for the thermal layout of IGCT driver board components. Firstly, according to the requirements of the IGCT electrical characteristics, the driver board is divided into functional regions. Secondly, based on the size, adjacent spacing and heat flux gradient of the main heating components in each region, the displacement is iterated until the final layout results are output when the termination conditions are met. Finally, the simulation comparison results of the proposed and the traditional driver board show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the thermal performance of the IGCT driver board, realize the reasonable distribution of the overall temperature and reduce the local hot spot temperatures.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Global Sensitivity Analysis of Output Power to Electrical Faults in Different SPV Array Topologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The faults in a solar photovoltaic (SPV) array significantly impact the energy balance and system dependability. Lowered system efficiency, reduced output power, and fire risks result from SPV array faults. Evaluating the loss during high impedance array faults is difficult because of the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control and the blocking and bypass diodes employed in an SPV system. This article analyzes the output power reduction due to different electrical faults in an SPV array connected to a grid. Two different topologies of SPV array configuration, namely, series-parallel (SP) and total-cross-tied (TCT), have been analyzed to find out the sensitivity of power to various electrical faults such as line-to-line (LL) and line-to-ground (LG) at different fault resistances. Using minimal historical data, a data-based global sensitivity analysis using a Kriging-based metamodel approach is proposed to discover the hidden global relationship between output power to various electrical faults in an SPV array. Later, Sobol indices are calculated to assess the severity of faults. The proposed methodology is validated in a hardware set-up of a grid-connected SPV system. The evaluation of performance indicators suggests that SP topology is more efficient as compared to TCT at zero impedance faults, whereas, during high impedance faults, both topologies carry similar power losses.

articleTitle: Switched-Midpoint Boost Inverter (SMBI)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Existing three-level inverters such as T-type topology use two series-connected dc-link capacitors to generate three symmetric voltage levels. As their maximum voltage level is limited to only half dc-link voltage, they require a frontend boost converter to extend voltage gain that constitutes a two-stage topology. This paper introduces a 3-phase single-stage boost inverter termed as the Switched-Midpoint Boost Inverter (SMBI). The proposed topology facilitates control of the dc-link capacitors by incorporating a power switch at their midpoint. By enabling the parallel connection of the dc-link capacitors during charging by a boost inductor, voltage balance is naturally maintained, obviating the need for any voltage balancing controllers or sensors. For a given boost inductor charging duty-cycle, the dc-link voltage of the proposed SMBI is double compared to the conventional two-stage inverter, thus enhancing the voltage gain. Moreover, the proposed inverter effectively mitigates high-frequency common-mode voltage by establishing a common-ground structure through the direct connection of the ac neutral to the negative terminal of the dc source. The operating principle of the proposed SMBI is thoroughly analyzed and validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Solar PV Power Prediction System Based on Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Electricity power is an essential need for the development of technology and industries. It is an essential component of modern human life. Using fossil and other petroleum components for electricity generation harms the environment. Many countries and industries have started using renewable sources like solar systems for electrical power generation. However, the main inconvenience of these systems is that they are unpredictable. The purpose of this work is to develop a machine learning-based method to estimate the generated power of PV solar systems based on environmental data such as sun irradiation, wind speed, and others. Before implementing Machine Learning techniques, the built system goes through a feature selection stage to identify the most influential parts. This step improves system performance by removing unnecessary data. Only three ML approaches were used and compared: CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), SVR (Support Vector Regression), and (RF) Random Forest. The SVR outperforms the competition.

articleTitle: Calculation of DC Fault Current and Analysis of Influencing Factors in MMC-based Medium Voltage DC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The use of modular multilevel converters (MMCs) is an emerging trend in medium-voltage direct current (MVDC)-based transmission and distribution networks. In order to address possible dc faults in MVDC system, it is necessary to conduct fault analysis with numerical calculations. Since MVDC systems have more complicated topology structures and flexible source/load deployment, the conventional fault analysis method applied to the HVDC systems cannot be directly extended to MVDC networks. In this paper, an expanded RLC equivalent model is derived for state-space based analysis of fault current calculations. Results of MMC and branch currents in different cases reveal the unique characteristics in the MVDC system. The system fault level is evaluated and compared with respect to different influencing factors, i.e. fault locations and initial operating scenarios.

articleTitle: An Advanced Frequency Adaptive PLL for Grid Connected Inverters Under Abnormal Grid Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: There has been an emerging need to diversify the utilization of distributed renewable energy sources (DRES) with grid connected inverters (GCI). A key component in the GCI's controller is the quick and precise acquisition of the phase angle of grid voltage. Phase-locked loop (PLL) controller is usually used for phase angle extraction and its performance is very crucial in abnormal grid conditions, including frequency variations, harmonic pollutions, and imbalanced grid events. Frequency adaptive PLL (FAPLL) has gained popularity due to its light computational burden, faster phase angle detection, and excellent harmonic rejection at nominal grid frequency. Unfortunately, due to spectral leakage at abnormal frequencies/harmonics, FAPLL data bears inaccuracies in both magnitude and phase angle estimation. To resolve this problem, this study proposes an advanced FAPLL (AFAPLL), which can work under abnormal frequencies or harmonics and avoid spectral leakage by implementing a variable window length phase detector, even in the presence of high harmonics in the grid voltage. Through extensive simulation results under various abnormal grid conditions, the superior performance of the AFAPLL is validated.

articleTitle: Distributed Average Integral Control Based Energy Management Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: In this research study, we proposed a Distributed Average Integral (DAI) control-based Energy Management Model (EMM) to achieve the economic load dispatch and consensus within a distributed energy system. The proposed model incorporates the Laplacian graph theory for establishing communication among energy districts (acting as agents/nodes) and optimizing the power distribution while satisfying the load demand. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model, simulations are performed using MATLAB. The simulation results illustrate that the DAI control mechanism ensures the optimized power distribution leading to enhanced resource utilization while effectively achieving economic consensus among energy districts. However, in this study ideal case scenario is assumed. Therefore, this research study may highlight the potential for future investigations on utilizing the DAI control for EMM in practical scenarios with real-world challenges such as system complexities, losses, and communication delays.

articleTitle: Photovoltaics Maximum Power Tracking by the Hybrid Perturb-Observe and Sliding Mode Control Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: To increase photovoltaic PV power, the point of maximum power, MPPT, must be tracked effectively. The oscillation around the operating point is the main drawback of MPPT-obtaining techniques. This study suggests combining the Perturb and Observe, PO, and Sliding Mode Control, SMC, strategies to reduce this problem and deal with the nonlinearities of the solar panels under different climate situations. The SMC creates a sliding surface that establishes the operational point and increases the stability of the PO. The gate of a DC-DC converter quickly reaches this defined surface, and the duty cycle adjustment ensures maximum power in all conditions. This study utilized MATLAB/Simulink to design and analyze this combined control system. The outcomes supported the PO and SMC strategy’s reliability and successful operation under various environmental circumstances.

articleTitle: Enhancing Renewable Energy Integration: A Hybrid AHP-TOPSIS Approach for Optimal Inverter Selection in Solar PV and Wind Turbine Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The selection of appropriate inverters is pivotal in maximizing the efficiency and performance of solar photovoltaic and wind turbine systems, as they directly impact the overall energy conversion efficiency and system output by influencing efficiency and reliability. Inverter selection also encompasses critical criteria like cost, compatibility with renewable energy sources, and environmental considerations. Thus, an exhaustive and systematic approach is essential to effectively evaluate and compare different inverter options. This study employs multi-criteria decision-making to address these challenges, evaluating the identified criteria using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and ranking them to determine the optimal solution via Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Consequently, the investigation identifies smart grid and smart meter inverters as the ideal solutions, successfully addressing concerns regarding power stability, communication and connectivity, security, data management, and cost. The proposed methodology yields a substantial total equity portion of USD 9,325.71, accompanied by impressive earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) of USD 1,734.09 per year. The estimated payback period is 6.85 years, and the return on investment (ROI) reaches a remarkable 338.07%. Additionally, the net income significantly reduces the production cost, with USD 40,853.34 in a single period.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Peak Shaving Techniques with Battery Energy Storage System in Small-scale Electrical Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Due to the overgrowing electrical demand in power systems, the electrical networks and end-users are facing numerous problems, including high demand charges, power losses across the electrical networks, voltage-frequency imbalance, etc. The inclusion of battery energy storage systems (BESS) with electrical networks for demand minimization is a suitable solution to overcome these concerns to ensure optimal and economic power flow. In this paper, two different peak load shaving techniques namely, the Fixed Demand Limit (FDL) technique and Decision Tree based Peak Shaving Algorithm (DT-PSA), are assessed to find the potentiality of peak shaving performance. Both techniques can reduce peak demands in different prospects as they have advantages and limitations in real scenarios. The aim of this study is to evaluate the operational performance of these two strategies on peak shaving applications, i.e., whether they can fit in small-scale electrical networks to ensure economic and optimal operation. Various time-varying load profiles are applied in real scenarios for both techniques to evaluate their peak shaving performances. Simulation results exhibit the functionality of the strategies.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Operating Modes for a Quadratic Boost Derived Reconfigurable Three Port Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The architecture of quadratic boost dc-dc converters consists of two pairs of reactive elements and four semiconductor devices (active and passive) within the same topology. This work explores the possibility of refurnishing this converter topology with controlled switches to enable multi-source integration and achieve reconfigurability. The topology modification results in an integrated power converter, capable of interfacing two energy sources with one source bidirectional and potential applications in distributed power systems, and consumer electronics. The re-configurable nature of the power converter widens the scope of its operation, and in this work, multi-port integrability, and bidirectional power flow capability at the ports are evaluated. For the operation and control of the converter, pulse width modulation strategies for different operating modes have been proposed. The operating modes of the derived topologies, their control methods, and the demonstration of characteristic behavior have been presented in the work. Experimental results validate the operation of the converter in different modes of operation.

articleTitle: Energy Management in Integrated Microgrids: An Optimal Schedule Controller Utilizing Gradient Descent Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper presents a new optimal controller using the Binary Gradient Descent (BGD) algorithm to manage distributed generations effectively in a grid network. The algorithm aims to minimize power consumption from the main grid and prioritize sustainable resource utilization over buying electricity from the local network grid. The proposed approach is evaluated on the IEEE fourteen bus test system with integrated Microgrids (MGs) and distributed generations, using real load demand data from Perlis, Malaysia, for 24-hour test case studies. Weather data, including wind, solar, fuel, and battery status, is integrated into the BGD algorithm for optimizing ON and OFF schedules. The results demonstrate a significant 46.3% reduction in energy consumption achieved by the BGD algorithm, contributing to the advancement of optimization algorithms for sustainable energy management. The developed BGD algorithm's effectiveness is further validated through a comparative analysis with conventional methods.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Reactive Power Optimization Model for Distribution Grid with Renewables
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: High penetration of distributed renewables in the distribution grid has adverse effects on nodal voltage, network loss, and system stable operation. In order to address these adverse effects, this paper established a comprehensive reactive power optimization model via coordinating multiple reactive power compensation measures to achieve the optimal operation of the distribution power grid. The objective function minimizing the sum of voltage deviation, network loss, and economic cost is established firstly, the constraints of node voltage and branch current in the grid, the output constraints of access to new energy, and the reactive output constraints of Static Var Compensator (SVC) and Shunt compensation capacitor are also considered. Then, the comprehensive reactive power optimal mathematical model is solved by the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Finally, the simulation results of the IEEE33-bus distribution network verify the practicality of the proposed reactive power optimization strategy.

articleTitle: Smart Substation Control and Protection Facilitating the Virtualization of Multiple Protection and Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The protection of the power system component is crucial for the healthy and reliable operation of the entire grid. Depending upon the equipment being protected and the type of fault it may encounter, various protection functions are employed. This paper proposes the centralized protection and control (CPC) technique which represents an innovative strategy that consolidates all protection and control functions within a single device at the substation level. The implementation of the CPC strategy eliminates the need for protection relays in each feeder and transformer bay within the substation. This offers the utility the flexibility to optimize space in the control room by reducing the number of control and relay panels required. Moreover, it offers a unified interface for monitoring and controlling power system components. This functionality simplifies the ability to effectively protect and oversee a wide range of utility and industrial applications through a single device, ensuring seamless visibility throughout the entire station. This streamlines engineering tasks and ensures a straightforward and cost-effective process management approach.

articleTitle: Transnational Federated Testbed: Analyzing Impact of Network Parameters on T&D Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) into the power system increases the size requirement of the models to induce actual system characteristics, since the simplification of sections of the model as lump load or source may result into misleading conclusions during dynamic and transient conditions. Growing interest on studying of DERs connected grids is enormously risen to investigate present and future systematic issues in dealing with natural and forced outages. This causes a new resource problem for smaller research organizations, utilities and vendors as more expensive, real-time simulators must be purchased to sufficiently simulate large enough models. However, researchers have built communication tools that allow labs to pool their resources by connecting their individual real-time simulators, emulators, and real DER assets together through the internet, allowing them to co-simulate larger/more detailed models that were previously too large for their individual labs. There is a limited focus on the impact of communication delays on federated co-simulation test beds. The main contribution of this work is to analyze the effect of the data rate and latent communication that are used to connect the two labs during the co-simulated transient events. The results are verified by running a co-simulated event on RTDS at Washington State University (WSU) in Pullman, Washington, and the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur(IITK) in Kanpur, India, by comparing the simulated measurements of the connection between the transmission and distribution systems in both simulations and finding the error between those sets of measurements. Further, it investigates different faults on the distribution system and provides the optimal data rate to achieve the best accuracy of dynamic simulations running at dispersed locations.

articleTitle: Effect of AC COP and Energy Tariff on Space Cooling Energy Consumption in Hot Climate Regions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the effect of having efficient and inefficient air conditioning (AC) units on the total energy needed for space cooling in hot climate regions, Saudi Arabia as an example. In such hot climate regions, space cooling is used extensively and accounts for a significant percentage of energy cost. It is inevitable to not face this challenge. One way to face it is through different tariff and increased AC units efficiency. The efficiency of an AC unit is expressed in terms of coefficient of performance (COP). In addition, there are different pricing schemes; however, two pricing structures were used; namely: block and time-of-use (TOU) structures. A case study was demonstrated for summer months in Saudi Arabia. TOU tariff resulted in less total energy consumption; however, higher kW demand compared with block tariff system for the same COP value. Finally, the Probabilistic Production Costing (PPC) method was utilized to evaluate the reliability of the system. The PPC showed that when applying TOU, reliability worsened slightly compared to block tariff system for the same COP value. Overall, the study showed that efficient AC could have a greater effect on reducing the demand than imposing a tariff such as TOU tariff.

articleTitle: Development of A Demand Control Algorithm for HVAC Systems to Conserve Energy in Office Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: In developing countries, rapid growth in new building constructions has driven a substantial increase in energy demand over the past decade. As buildings account for 40% of a country's total energy consumption, optimising energy performance while ensuring occupants' comfort has become imperative. Within this sector, Heating, Ventilation & Air-Conditioning (HVAC) systems alone contribute over 40% of energy consumption in office buildings. This study addresses the timely need to reduce energy consumption by developing an occupancy-based demand control algorithm for HVAC systems in office buildings. An algorithm was developed to integrate the Building Management System with the door access control system database, facilitated by a Modbus controller. This controller translates the occupancy rate into an analogue signal, modulating the blower motor speed of Air Handling Units via the Building Management System software. The study also quantifies the potential energy savings the new algorithm achieves in the context of office buildings in Sri Lanka. Preliminary findings suggest that the developed algorithm could lead to up to 75% energy savings in HVAC systems. By considering the occupancy level and the status of a building, such as the presence or absence of the occupants, this algorithm optimises energy use while maintaining occupants' well-being. The proposed methodology has the potential to offer substantial energy savings and contribute to sustainable building practices in developing countries.

articleTitle: A Single Phase Multilevel Inverter with Reduced Component Count and Enhancing Performance Parameter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Efficient and cost-effective power converters are essential in modern power applications. A viable solution for low and medium-voltage applications is multilevel inverters (MLIs). However, the widespread adoption of MLIs has been limited due to challenges such as a high number of switches, larger physical size, increased costs, complex control requirements, and multi-stage power conversion losses in switching conduction. Despite their promising role in industrial applications, these factors have hindered the market penetration of MLIs. This research offers a generalize single-phase direct converted multilevel inverter where the proposed MLI topology achieves a significant reduction in semiconductor components count rather than conventional topologies, minimizes physical weight and overall cost. The propose topology uses less number of switching conduction in every single mode which reduces the significant amount of switching loss as well as the control complexity. Optimal THD effectiveness for output voltage and current is assured by the use of unipolar modulation. Simulation results conducted in MATLAB/Simulink validate the viability of the suggested topology, while a comparative analysis with traditional inverter and the modern inverter topology highlights its advantages. A scaled-down laboratory prototype circuit board is designed to assure the feasibility. Results from both experiments and simulations show that the suggested topology is feasible and has many great qualities.

articleTitle: Power Quality Problem for Single–Phase Low–Voltage Charging of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The paper discusses power quality (PQ) issues related to the charging process (CP) of an electric vehicle (EV) traction battery by the single-phase on–board low–voltage charger. The monitored on-board charger is configured to provide a constant current value. During monitoring, the focus has been paid on identification of the CP impact on PQ. The results of the research carried out show that the monitored EV CP is multistage. Variations in current, power, and content of higher harmonics and supraharmonics are observed. From a PQ point of view, the parameters of the power network at the point of connection of an on–board EV charger have a direct impact on the effects of such changes. Knowledge of the nature of changes at various stages of the CP makes it possible to identify such sources of disturbance in power networks. The results of the experiments show the need for uninterruptible monitoring of PQ in the supply circuit of electrical devices that are sensitive to poor PQ.

articleTitle: Impact of Large-scale EVs Integration on Small Signal Stability of Renewable-Rich Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: A large-scale electric vehicles (EVs) integration will result in different load profiles depending on the charging strategy being used. Consequently, this will have an impact on the dynamic behavior of the power system. This manuscript aims to examine the impact of uncontrolled, uncontrolled with photovoltaic (PV), and time-of-use (TOU) based tariff charging strategies on dynamic performance of the transmission networks, specifically the small signal stability. The proposed methodology is applied within an IEEE 9-bus system enriched with renewable energy sources (RESs). This study illustrates the impact of different EV penetration levels ranging from 0% to 100% on small signal stability of power system, particularly under conditions of low system strength. The results indicate that the increasing EV charging load may deteriorate the system stability if the charging process is not properly managed.

articleTitle: Coordinated Operation of Coupled Transportation and Energy System based on Modified User Equilibrium Assignment Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Electric vehicles play a vital role in reducing carbon emissions and mitigating climate change. With the aim of encouraging the adoption of electric vehicles, this paper proposes a coordinated operation model of the coupled transportation and energy system based on a modified user equilibrium assignment model. The modified user equilibrium model innovatively considers the feature of electric vehicles and the impact of charging facilities on electric vehicle flow distribution. In addition, the influence of the electric vehicle charging time and queuing time on the vehicle flow assignment is also considered. According to the flow assignment result obtained by the modified user equilibrium model, the coordinated operation model of the coupled transportation and power system is proposed to minimize the total cost. A system integrated with a power-gas coupled energy network and a 12-node transportation network coupled with 5 charging facilities is employed to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated operation model.

articleTitle: Assessment of Backup Generator Connection Barriers to Australian Medium Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Demand response (DR) programs can benefit electricity consumers, distribution network service providers (DNSPs), system operators and the energy market. However, the complexity and characteristics associated with loads connected to customer premises, utilisation of backup generators for DR and the baseline calculation process still require considerable research to optimise and further unlock the capabilities of DR programs. This paper analyses the barriers to using backup generators in medium voltage (MV) networks in DR programs. Two representative Australian MV networks (e.g., Urban-NSW1 network, Urban-VIC network) are analysed in DIgSILENT PowerFactory under different scenarios, such as variation in locations, power export limits, and dynamic export limits of backup generators. The study has found that a backup generator located at the end of the network can achieve better performance in supporting the network voltage. Moreover, the voltage limit and thermal limit of the power network mainly constrain the export limits of backup generators. Furthermore, a backup generator with a dynamic export limit can export 1 to 5 times more energy than the static export limit.

articleTitle: Allocation of EV Charging Stations in a Micro-grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Thanks to appropriately located and sized Distributed Generation (DG) units a significant reduction in power losses and improved voltage stability has been witnessed in power systems in recent times. The optimal location of an Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS) needs special attention to cope with the increase in the number of Electric Vehicle (EVs), Energy management during charging and discharging in Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) modes of operation has gained attraction among power engineers on the integration of EVs into smart distribution systems (DS). The DG helps maintain a voltage profile within acceptable bounds, which reduces power flows and losses and improves power quality and dependability. In this context, this research develops a single objective to reduce Active Power Losses (APL) and enhance bus voltage profiles in the DS. The Hybrid TLBO-PSO algorithm is used to solve the optimization problem. The strategy for minimizing losses presented in this study uses many DGs situated in the best possible way and various EVCS Levels that can operate in both G2V and V2G modes. Considering different scenarios, the proposed algorithm is evaluated on IEEE 33 and IEEE 69 bus network. The outcomes demonstrate that Hybrid TLBO-PSO offers the best solution with minimal APL and an enhanced voltage profile.

Author Keywords: Hybrid Teaching Learning Based Particle Swarm Optimization

articleTitle: Electrical vehicle charging strategy for electric road systems considering V2G technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The accelerated adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) introduces a substantial amount of load to the power grid. The electric road system (ERS) emerged as a promising solution to decarbonize heavy good vehicles and extend the driving range of EVs, will further complicate the operation of power grid. Therefore, optimal scheduling of EV charging in ERS is vital in minimizing the impact of variable EV loads to the power grid that provides power supply to the ERS. This paper proposes a charging strategy based on load floating (LOF) electricity price. The approach divides a day into different time periods, counting the grid-connected and off-grid time of vehicles, and then establish dispatching and charging cost models, based on which the EV charging cost is minimized. The simulation results confirm the efficiency of the proposed scheduling strategy.

articleTitle: Locating Faults with Ease- A Fault Current Matching Method for Distribution Feeders
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Locating faults in large distribution networks presents a major challenge due to limited measurement data. Deploying smart sensors in the network could improve network observability, but they pose significant techno-economic challenges. To overcome this limitation, the paper proposes a cost-effective fault current-matching technique that estimates fault location using network data and fault resistance. First, the method finds the possible fault line sections between adjacent protective devices and calculates the theoretical fault current for each line. Then, the calculated fault currents are compared with measured values using a fault expectancy index, resulting in a compilation of prospective fault locations with corresponding possibilities. To validate the proposed method, two recent fault events in two different feeders recorded from actual distribution grids in New South Wales (NSW), Australia, are used. The method classifies the fault accurately and detects faulted line sections with more than 90 percent fault expectancy based on the test cases. The proposed approach offers an efficient solution to techno-economic challenges, potentially enhancing fault detection and service restoration efforts.

articleTitle: A Loss Reduction Formulation for Capacitor Placement in Reconfigurable Distribution Grids with Variable Electricity Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Reducing network losses through hybrid system reconfiguration and placement of shunt capacitors subject to time-varying electricity consumption is a combinatorial optimization problem, which needs significant numerical attempts in real distribution networks. For intricacy decrease, majority of previously published works in the field did not consider variability of load, even though this ignorance may increase the solutions inaccuracy. For this issue, current paper presents an efficient model to formulate variable loads in a large-scale hybrid problem of network reconfiguration and reactive power controller placement. Implementation of the approach proposed in present paper on several example systems demonstrates the correctness, quick computational processing, and easy application in comparison with traditional based-peak load models and variable load-based formulations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Flux Cancellation Zone in Inductive Power Transfer for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Over the past decade, there has been a growing adoption of Electric vehicles (EVs) in the transportation industry. However, the pivotal problem of charging the EV battery remains to be a big obstacle in this sector. To tackle the energy storing challenges involved in EVs, Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) has drawn a significant attention in the literature. However, in WPT the efficiency of energy transmission is greatly affected by the coupling between the transmitter and receiver coils. This article investigates the "Flux Cancellation Zone" phenomenon that occurs at a certain area when the two coils are misaligned. Three types of coils, namely circular, square-shaped, and DD pads are studied to compare their performance. Various factors such as coil dimension, misalignment tolerance, winding spacing, and adding ferrite have been included to achieve the optimum results. It is concluded that using ferrite improves the coupling coefficient and can mitigate the problem in DD coils. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) tool has been employed using Ansys Electronics software to simulate and visualize the flux paths and coupling alterations.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Discharge Characteristics of Metal-Enclosed Liquid Nitrogen Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride(SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) is widely used in high-voltage circuit breakers due to its excellent insulation capability. At high temperatures, SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> tends to break down and produce toxic gases, which exacerbates the greenhouse impact. Given its excellent insulating qualities and environmental friendliness, liquid nitrogen(LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has the potential to replace other insulating materials in circuit breakers in the future. In this paper, metal-enclosed LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switching discharge characteristics are simulated by altering three conditions: electrode shape, electrode material, and LN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> temperature. The experiments were conducted using DC and various electrode spacings based on local thermodynamic equilibrium(LTE), and eventually changes in potential and pressure inside the closed cavity were noticed. The experimental results found that the sphere symmetric electrode has the lowest potential mean value at the small gap, meanwhile, the rod-sphere electrode has the lowest electric potential mean value at the large gap. In addition, the average value of pressure inside the chamber using the rod electrode was the lowest. The average rate of change of simulated electric potential and pressure was always the lowest using electrodes made of stainless steel.

articleTitle: Estimating Electric Vehicle Hosting Capacity in Distribution Networks: A Scalable Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative and scalable approach for estimating the hosting capacity for Electric Vehicles(EVs) in distribution networks. Excessive EV penetration causes detrimental impacts such as voltage fluctuations, power loss, voltage unbalance, and thermal overloading. Determining EV hosting is essential to maintain technical and operational constraints within statutory limits. This research considers multiple performance constraints with a streamlined approach for assessing EV hosting capacity in distribution networks. The result shows voltage fluctuation dominates over other indexes in all scenarios for the standard test network, whereas voltage unbalances dominate during minimum load scenarios for real distribution feeders. The proposed approach can help network operators to estimate EV hosting capacity in distribution networks, enabling efficient planning and optimization of charging infrastructure while ensuring reliable and secure grid operation.

articleTitle: Single Switch Dual Output Modified Zeta Converter fed SRM for Domestic Appliances
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: A modified Zeta-based single switch dual output converter with a mid-point is presented to drive switched reluctance motor (SRM) based low power appliances while maintaining grid power quality. In household appliances, cost and efficiency are major concerns. For even phases SRM, a midpoint converter requires a single switch and a single diode for magnetization and demagnetization for each phase. Discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) of operation is preferred over continuous conduction mode (CCM) due to least sensor count at cost of switch and diode voltages and current stress. Presented front-end modified zeta converter regulates DC link voltage and preserves grid’s functionality with low total harmonics distortion (THD) as per international standards (IEEE 519-2023/ IEC 61000-3-2). Speed of SRM-based appliances is controlled by regulating mid-point split DC link voltages. In voltage-controlled operation of SRM drive, speed sensor is additionally eliminated. A zeta-derived converter is described to facilitate balanced split DC link voltage, which is needed for mid-point converter of SRM. Split DC output modified zeta converter’s reliability, for SRM fed, is assessed using a 600 W SRM drive, and simulation outcomes endorse converter’s authenticity.

articleTitle: Improving Frequency Regulation in Power Systems via Noisynet Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The growing utilization of renewable energy resources in contemporary power systems has presented challenges for conventional model-based load frequency control (LFC) methods. These challenges include the escalation of computational burdens and diminished control performance. In order to address the stochastic disturbances, a novel approach called the Noisynet Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) method is proposed to adjust the agent’s parameters. Comparative analysis between the proposed method, the conventional DDPG method, and a finely-tuned PID method demonstrates that the proposed method yields a superior control policy. Consequently, the Noisynet DDPG method shows significant promise as a means to enhance LFC performance.

articleTitle: Optimal Reconfiguration of Radial Distribution Networks Using PSO-CRO Approach for Loss Minimization and Voltage Stability Enhancement under Voltage Dependent Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper manifests the static Voltage Stability Assessment (VSA), voltage deviation measurement, and loss reduction determination of voltage-dependent load model-based Radial Distribution System (RDS). The performance parameters for voltage stability assessment are calculated by the load flow method. A hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization-Coral Reef Optimization (PSO-CRO) approach is proposed for optimal network reconfiguration that significantly enhances voltage stability margin and reduces power loss in addition with voltage deviations at buses from desired values not only under Constant Power (CP) load but under a variety of voltage-dependent loads. Simulations are performed on IEEE 33-bus RDS for the unreconfigured case as well as optimally reconfigured case through a PSO-CRO based approach. A comparative study of simulation results obtained for both cases establishes the efficacy of PSO-CRO based network reconfiguration and the importance of consideration of voltage-dependent loads.

articleTitle: Small-signal Stability Analysis of Offshore DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: DC microgrids are becoming an attractive option for offshore applications owing to their capability to incorporate various distributed energy sources. However, connecting all generating units, storage systems, and loads to DC microgrids via multiple converters can lead to system instability. DC bus voltage may fluctuate based on load changes, converter operating conditions, and controller tuning. Therefore, maintaining voltage stability over a broad limit of operations poses a significant challenge for offshore DC MGs. To address this challenge, this paper presents mathematical models of various DC microgrid components and proposes a suitable controller design to ensure system stability. The designed cascaded controller is demonstrated to successfully control the voltage on the bus while maintaining overall system stability for a small DC microgrid simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. The system's performance has been validated by Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) simulations for small-signal stability analysis. The system's stability is analyzed, assessing transient responses, frequency responses, and the sensitivity of the small-signal model.

articleTitle: State feedback with observers for DC-DC converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: DC-DC converters are widely used in various applications, including renewable energy integration and electric transport. Performance of DC-DC converters can be improved through using advanced control methods. This paper introduces state feedback control with state and disturbance observers for a buck converter. The paper includes detailed mathematical modelling in both continuous-time and discrete-time domains, as well as detailed design of the observer and control parameters. The paper compares performance of state feedback control and PI control and shows advantages of the former. Detailed simulations in MATLAB/Simulink environment validate the paper findings.

articleTitle: Adequacy Assessment of a Distribution Network Embedded with Combined Solar PV and Hydrogen Storage Based PEM Fuel Cell System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The incorporation of solar photovoltaic (PV) along with hydrogen storage within power distribution systems offers a promising solution to mitigate the intermittency in PV outputs and holds the potential to enhance the overall system operational efficiency. Reliability assessment is crucial to measure the influence of combined PV and hydrogen storage based PEM fuel cell system on the distribution networks. This paper proposes an innovative approach to assess the proportion of the load demand met by fuel cells during high demand periods and the level of grid reliance for a distribution system incorporating PV and hydrogen systems. The results demonstrate a considerable improvement in the newly proposed reliability indices for the sample distribution network demonstrating effectiveness of integrating the combined PV and fuel cell system.

articleTitle: Cost Effective Analysis of Stationary and Mobile Energy Storage Systems in Prosumer Microgrid Considering System Reliability and Real-Time Pricing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The energy demand is increasing especially in the urban areas. Various sources of energy are used to fulfill the energy demand. The fossil fuel is depleting and prices of the energy is increasing all over the world. On the other side, energy crises are the main concern of developing countries. Energy is a need in every field of human life, such as in industrial, commercial, residential, and educational institutes. The proposed system is comprised of the solar PV, electric vehicle (EV), utility grid and energy storage system. Prosumer Microgrid is analyzed in literature but ignores mobile and stationary energy storages with real time pricing and reliability. This paper analyzed the campus microgrid with the exchange of energy with the utility grid using the intelligent energy management system (IEMS). Different types of Distributed Generation (DG) with utility grid are integrated and analyzed and reduced operational cost by 74 % which shows the significance of the obtained results. The proposed model is linear and solved using linear programming considering real time pricing scheme. The proposed model can be implemented for the establishment of the smart building.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Compensation from Single-Phase Low Voltage Inverter Based Resources to Improve Voltage Stability in the Australian Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The energy landscape in Australia is undergoing a significant transformation, characterized by the growing adoption of consumer energy resources (CER), particularly rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, and the retirement of traditional synchronous generators in favour of grid-scale inverter-based resources (IBR) such as wind and solar. This transition brings about fundamental changes to the operation of the Australian power system, with system strength emerging as a critical concern. While synchronous generators are inherently a strong source of system strength, IBR, by contrast, are a weaker source that require external compensation. As the retirement of synchronous generators progresses, Australia is beginning to witness system strength issues, resulting in the need for network operators to procure costly compensation services. This paper investigates the potential of single-phase CER, prevalent in many Australian households, to provide compensation. If proven successful, this will replace the need for some amount of costly compensation, reducing the energy bills of the end consumer. To test this, a single-phase CER model was developed in PSCAD/EMTDC, to provide compensation during a disturbance. Results show that the proposed reactive power injection scheme provides marginally better results than the Volt-VAr characteristics in AS/NZS 4777.2:2020, and is significantly more effective than a case with no compensation.

articleTitle: Aggregator-Driven Novel Battery Scheduling: Orchestrating Demand in a Grid Dominated by Distributed Photovoltaics and Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology to schedule community-level aggregator-controlled battery energy storage (BESS) to counteract the variability of distributed photovoltaic (D-PV) generation and electric vehicle (EV) demand. There is an increasing need to address the variability introduced by D-PV and EV adoption. This variability can lead to challenges like increased operation complexities and reduced efficiency of power distribution. This paper introduces a novel BESS scheduling approach tailored for community-level aggregators. The goal is to shape the grid operator’s demand profile, achieving valley filling and peak shaving without compromising operational costs. The scheduling algorithm is a convex optimisation problem, which was solved using the interior point method to intelligently decide the charging and discharging rate at each time interval. Simulator tests show significant cost reductions of up to 50%. The study shows that the proposed BESS scheduling algorithm can help to create an operator-friendly demand curve while minimising the aggregator cost.

articleTitle: Improved Deadtime Compensation Method Considering Currrent Ripple
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: In various deadtime compensation methodologies, the waveform of deadtime compensation voltage (DTCV) is subject to the influence of current polarity. A prevalent approach involves employing rotor position for an estimation of the fundamental current phase. Yet, it is crucial to acknowledge that the precise zero-crossing point of the current is susceptible to the effects of the current ripple arising from switching events. This paper introduces a novel technique that enhances the performance of deadtime compensation by considering the impact of current ripple. The magnitude of the current ripple is deduced through meticulous circuit analysis. Subsequently, a calculated time shift, derived from the characteristics of the current ripple, is applied to the fundamental zero-crossing time. This adjustment contributes to a more accurate estimate of the actual zero-crossing time. The efficacy of the method is evaluated through simulations conducted in SIMULINK using a high-speed Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) as the test platform. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly diminishes both current ripple and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the phase current. These enhancements are particularly pronounced, especially during high-speed operational scenarios.

articleTitle: Carbon tax utility analysis based on multi-objective optimization and market equilibrium in power system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: The current power system is grappling with substantial challenges in achieving lower carbon emissions. To tackle this issue, various policy instruments such as carbon taxes, Renewable Portfolio Standards, and carbon markets have been proposed. In this context, the primary aim of this paper is to assess the impact of carbon taxes on reducing carbon emissions and their influence on the overall efficiency of the power market. This study employs a bi-level model to derive the game equilibrium solution of the power market through fixed-point iteration. Furthermore, the normal boundary intersection method is employed to address the multi-objective optimization problem, which takes into account both generation costs and carbon emissions. This approach leads to the identification of the Pareto frontier and reveals the emission reduction potential of the power system. Through varying the magnitude of the carbon tax, sensitivity analysis is carried out, and simulations using the IEEE 30-node dataset demonstrate that carbon taxes can effectively curtail carbon emissions within the power generation system. However, it is worth noting that under certain conditions, a penalty-based carbon tax mechanism may encounter challenges in achieving the goal of carbon emission reduction.

articleTitle: A Planning Model for Optimal Capacity and Location of Energy Storage for Grid Inertial Support in Presence of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Energy Technologies for Future Grids (ETFG)
abstract: Due to the concerns over the environment and the limitations of natural resources, the penetration of renewable energy resources (RESs) is expected to increase dramatically in the upcoming years.
